No suspicious object has been found during searches so far, they said.
Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in Lodi Estate, Venkateshwar Global School in Rohini, and Salwan Public School in Mayur Vihar received the threat emails, following which authorities were informed.
Delhi Fire Service said teams rushed to the schools after receiving information about the threats, and the premises were evacuated as a precautionary measure.
Bomb disposal squads, dog squads, fire department and police personnel are conducting searches at the premises, officials said.
Investigation is underway to trace the source of the threat emails, they added.

articles.title: 2,700 detained amid riots & looting in France
articles.summary: French police have taken 2,700 people into custody since Saturday in connection with riots and looting, Reuters reported citing Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin, as authorities brace for further unrest across the country."Some 2,700 people have been taken into police custody since Saturday in connection with these riots and looting," Darmanin said in an interview with French news channel LCI.French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be prohibited in the coming days. He blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, Macron said demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be permitted, although authorities could divert them to alternative routes to protect businesses."Last Saturday we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic," he said.His remarks came as authorities across France prepared for fresh protests following some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.Darmanin said he wanted voting rights to be suspended for people who violate bans on demonstrations. He also called for restrictions on social media access for those involved in violence, looting or attacks on police.Authorities have banned all protests scheduled for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities. However, new demonstrations are already being planned ahead of a weekend that officials fear could turn volatile.France's main student union, UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, has submitted plans for a march through central Paris.Businesses in central Paris have started boarding up their shop windows in anticipation of possible violence. Luxury goods group Hermes said it had strengthened security at its stores across France.Organisers of Art Basel Paris, an international art collectors fair being held in an exhibition hall in central Paris, said the event would remain closed throughout the weekend.In the northern city of Orleans, authorities were preparing for possible unrest as the far-right National Rally prepared to hold its annual meeting, while unions and left-wing groups planned demonstrations.A student protest scheduled for Thursday in Paris was initially banned but was later permitted to proceed. However, transit authorities shut metro stations in central Paris in anticipation of unauthorised gatherings.PUBLIC ANGERFrance was shaken by violence on the fringes of nationwide protests on October 17, exposing the extent of public anger and raising concerns about the ability of security services to maintain order.Two people have been arrested in connection with an arson attack on the city hall in Limoges, according to French officials and media reports.A third consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas affected by the violence, giving the government some respite ahead of the weekend.The unrest has also exposed deeper discontent in France, where rising energy costs, mounting pressure on household budgets and concerns about deteriorating public services have fuelled frustration among workers and younger people.France's political class has meanwhile become embroiled in a bitter blame game, with the government accusing far-left political groups of fuelling the unrest.(With inputs from Reuters)

articles.title: 7.0 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16
articles.summary: Beijing: A strong earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 46 in China's remote Tibet region, state media said, citing local authorities.More than 300 houses collapsed in the 7.0 magnitude quake, which struck on Thursday at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT).Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, state news agency Xinhua said.China Central Television (CCTV) put the number of injured at 46, 11 of them seriously, with 339 houses collapsed or damaged, citing local officials.Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck.The epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.It struck at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres.A level-III earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, CCTV reported.The epicentre was in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.More than 300 police officers have been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported.Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, and carrying one person, footage on CCTV showed.It also showed rescue workers shining flashlights on other damaged buildings and soldiers lining up ready to be deployed.Earthquakes in China are relatively common.In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet's rural Tingri county.In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China killed at least 127 people, according to state media.That quake was China's deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the southwestern province of Yunnan.A huge tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left some 90,000 people dead or missing, including around 5,000 schoolchildren.

articles.title: ITBP DG gives a peek into troops' LAC plan
articles.summary: New Delhi: The ITBP has raised drone platoons in all its border units, prepared a new 'Strike' course to better handle Galwan-like battles and is creating underground infrastructure along the front "in a big way" as part of the new warfare to counter India's "biggest adversary" China, the force's chief said on Thursday.ITBP Director General (DG) Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor told his troops at a force base in Rajasthan's Alwar that countering China through "traditional" means of warfare was a thing of the past and hence they were investing in modernizing the force, its weapons, vehicles and border posts.The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), raised in 1962, guards the 3,488-km-long Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.The DG noted that the recent Ukraine-Russia and Iran-US wars have shown the importance of drone and anti-drone technology through which a small country can overwhelm a bigger nation during conflict.Also read | Army invites applications for 75-day internship programme in defence technologiesKapoor, who is set to retire from service on October 31, addressed his troops during an investiture ceremony held leading up to the force's 65th Raising Day on October 24.He said the China front was our "most difficult" border, and China was a "powerful" neighbour and India's "biggest adversary," requiring enhanced capabilities to "counter" it."Drones have become a major challenge and an opportunity also. It will be difficult to compete with China using traditional methods... They have modernised and invested heavily in their PLA but drones are such that a small country can give a befitting contest to a bigger nation," he said.He noted that almost 10,000-15,000 Russian troops are killed in the war with Ukraine every month."This is despite the fact that it (Russia) is a big country and a superpower. They (Russia) thought that they would capture (Ukraine) in 1-2 months but it is the fourth year counting, and every month they (Russians) have 10-15 thousand bodies reaching them," the DG said.He added that this caused such "big damage" and that Russia was suffering because of that one decision.Kapoor then cited the Iran-US war as an example, noting that Iran, without an Air Force, Navy, or Army, engaged in combat with the global superpower.Also read | From 290-km BrahMos to a proposed 1,500-km variant: How Operation Sindoor boosted India's missile profile"The role of traditional armies has changed since the drones arrived, and we must embrace drone and anti-drone systems in a big way," he said.Kapoor said the approximately 95,000-personnel-strong, mountain-warfare-trained ITBP has received government funds worth Rs 400 crore and 70 per cent of these funds have been earmarked for enhancing the force's drone warfare capabilities."Each border guarding battalion now has a drone platoon, and we are training drone pilots and building drones too.""The Ministry of Home Affairs has also granted in-principle approval to a bigger modernisation scheme of Rs 4,000 crore, of which we will earmark Rs 1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems," the DG said.He informed the troops that a new course named 'Strike' has been developed to train ITBP personnel, which will enhance their capabilities to face Galwan-like situations. The entire force will undergo this training by the end of 2027.Chinese soldiers used stones, nail-studded sticks, iron rods and clubs while carrying out brutal attacks on Indian soldiers along the LAC at Galwan (Ladakh) in June, 2020 resulting in 20 casualties on the Indian side while China belatedly claimed only 4 of its troops were killed. Multiple reports suggested that the Chinese fatalities were much higher.The ITBP chief added that a new combat team, the Shaurya commandos, has been raised. This team displayed its skills during the "ongoing" faceoff with the Chinese PLA troops at multiple places in Arunachal Pradesh.These commandos will be in every border battalion and will give the force a distinct identity, he said.The DG said the force was constructing underground shelters (bunkers) at border locations "in a big way," learning from the lessons of the new warfare, as above-ground buildings can become a target in 'hot war' situations, indicating the post-Operation Sindoor conflict with Pakistan.He said a pilot project is underway in this context and they plan to have these under-ground shelters in the coming years, equipped with the same comfort available in above-ground buildings.Kapoor said the force also worked on the ensuring the comfort and operational prepardeness of the troops by insulating 342 out of 383 barracks present in areas which face "sub-zero" temperatures, has procured 141 generator sets to ensure electricity at remote troop locations and got solar water heaters installed at a number of such facilities."This will help enhance the morale and confidence of the troops and improve the ITBP's operational preparedness," he said.The DG added that a 'cold start kit' was provided to border units which helps vehicles get immediate ignition in icy weather."Many years ago when we were in Kosovo in sub zero temperatures the vehicles there used to start in one crank. We wondered why this wasn't happening here? We did some experiments and now we can do it," he said.The DG also asked his troops to keep fit and healthy, saying a new diet plan has been introduced in the force and the "very high" content of sugar and oil has been lessened.He expressed concern over the cases of Alcohol Dependence Syndrome (ADS) in the ITBP which have doubled or tripled since 2020.The DG also asked the troops to be cautious against ADS and 'honey trap' instances of being lured by someone into sharing sensitive information through the social media.He added that the ITBP was also modernising its weapons, some of which are about 50 years old, and improving mobility through the procurement of new all-terrain Vehicles, ground vehicles and quick reaction vehicles,We have prepared a plan to become a specialised high-altitude mountain fighting force through all these measures, Kapoor said.

articles.title: Wall Street dumps AI for Buffett’s Berkshire
articles.summary: For three weeks, Wall Street sold one of the market’s hottest trades and bought one of its oldest. Chip stocks fell about 15 per cent. Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway rose about 7 per cent.Between October 2 and October 20, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) lost 15.1 per cent, while Berkshire’s Class B shares (BRK-B) gained 7.4 per cent, according to Yahoo Finance.On Tuesday, BRK-B closed at a record high for the first time since May 2, 2025, the day before Buffett said Greg Abel would take over as CEO.On Wednesday, both the Class B and Class A (BRK-A) shares touched new intraday records.Berkshire hits a record as chip stocks slump 15%: the rare dot-com-era signal investors are watching, and what it may mean for your portfolioThe wait was long. In those 17 months, the S&P 500 gained more than 35 per cent, and Berkshire only now got back to a record close.The recent moves have been strikingly one-sided. From October 6 to Tuesday, SOXX fell in 10 of 11 sessions, and Berkshire rose on nine of those days.On the chip sector’s two worst days, October 14 and October 16, Berkshire posted two of its best gains of the run. Since October 1, the stock has mostly gone up on days when chips went down.For now, that makes Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade.Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. It also strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018.The gap between the two is historic too. Over the 12 sessions from October 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points.Yahoo Finance compared Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index going back to 1994, and found this is the widest 12-session gap since early 2010. The all-time record, set in April 2000, was close to 40 points.The gap alone is not the rarest part. The combination is. Chips fell at least 14 per cent while Berkshire gained at least 7 per cent over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened on October 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, when the dot-com bubble was bursting.History gives a mixed message from here. In the short term, chips bounced back. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they are rebounding on Wednesday as well. A year later, the picture was weaker: chips were lower in five of six cases, and the S&P 500 fell in four.Under Abel, Berkshire is also using its cash differently. It bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter. That ended 14 straight quarters in which it sold more of its own stock than it bought, and its cash pile has come down from a record $397 billion.Buffett said on September 18 that he would step down as chairman too. The stock hit its low about two weeks later.The tech bets are changing as well. A few years ago, Apple made up nearly 45 per cent of Berkshire’s invested assets. Buffett was never known as a tech investor. What drew him to Apple was customer loyalty and people’s willingness to pay premium prices for iPhones, Macs and iPads, not the technology itself.In just a few months, Alphabet has become for Abel what Apple was for Buffett. Google handled roughly 90 per cent of global internet search traffic in September, which is part of the appeal. But the AI ambitions are what interest both men most. Since Alphabet added generative AI and large language models to Google Cloud, the world’s third-largest cloud platform, sales in that high-margin business have grown very fast.Abel is also looking beyond Alphabet. An October 14 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows Berkshire is buying 10 million shares of Bending Spoons in a private placement at $33 a share, an investment of $330 million. It follows a $600 million investment at the company’s IPO in July.The company’s model has some similarity to Berkshire’s own. Berkshire grew to a $1 trillion market value by buying about five dozen companies, and pieces of others, and usually holding them for a long time.Bending Spoons, based in Italy, buys technology platforms and uses software, AI, price hikes and layoffs to make them leaner and to sell more subscriptions. So far it has bought AOL, Vimeo, Brightcove, Eventbrite and WeTransfer, among others. The company is already profitable and growing quickly.The next test comes with Berkshire’s third-quarter results, expected on Saturday, November 7.
